title: Crashpad Near DFW Airport
excerpt: A quiet crashpad 7.5 miles from DFW Airport for commuting airline pilots. Cold beds from $330 a month, parking for your car, keyless entry, weekly cleaning. Apply online in two minutes.
content:
If you commute into DFW, the two things that matter most are how fast you can get from the gate to a bed, and whether that bed is yours. This crashpad is a house 7.5 miles from DFW Airport, about 15 minutes door to door outside of rush hour, and every bed in it is a cold bed.

What "near DFW" means here

  • 7.5 miles to the terminals. Close enough for an early show, far enough that you do not hear the airport.
  • Park your own car at the house. Room for 7 cars on the property, more on the street. No shuttle to time, no employee lot walk at 4 am.
  • Groceries within walking distance, plus bike and jogging trails nearby for the days you are not flying.

A cold bed, not a hot bed

Your bed is yours for the whole month, whether your schedule has you here three nights or every night. Nobody else sleeps in it. Pillow, sheets, blanket, and towel are provided, and your bed is made up before you arrive. Every bunk has a privacy curtain and an 8-inch memory foam mattress.

Pricing near DFW

  • Top bunk from $330 a month
  • Bottom bunk from $380 a month
  • Semi-private room (shared with one other crew member, no bunks) from $450
  • Private room from $475

Every price includes all utilities, Wi-Fi and streaming TV, a full kitchen with your own pantry and fridge space, free washer and dryer, weekly professional cleaning, and parking. There is a $150 reservation fee that is refundable after your first month. One-month minimum, then month to month. No 2 or 3 months up front.

How the door works

No keys. You unlock the front door with an app on your phone, any hour your trip ends. Your access is turned on before your move-in date and turned off when you leave.

Who stays here

Commuting airline pilots and crew who keep a permanent home somewhere else and need a clean, quiet place to sleep between trips at DFW. The house is kept quiet by people who understand early shows and late arrivals, because everyone here has them.

How to get a bed

  1. Apply online. It takes about two minutes.
  2. We text you to set up a short phone call.
  3. Sign online and pay the $150 reservation fee. Your bed is held.
  4. Get door access on your phone. Your bed is made when you arrive.

title: Crashpad for DFW-Based Airline Crews: American, Envoy, SkyWest, PSA
excerpt: Crew housing near DFW for pilots commuting to American Airlines, Envoy, SkyWest, PSA and other DFW-based operations. Month to month, cold beds from $330, 7.5 miles from the airport.
content:
DFW is one of the biggest pilot bases in the country, and most of the people who fly out of it do not live here. Whether you hold a line at American, sit reserve at Envoy, or just got based at DFW with SkyWest or PSA, you need somewhere to sleep that is close, clean, and does not lock you into a long lease. That is what this house is for.

Built around airline schedules

  • Month to month after the first month. Bases change, bids change. You are never stuck with 2 or 3 months paid up front.
  • Airline schedule exception on notice. If a bid award, base change, or reassignment lands after the 15th, tell us within 48 hours and your notice still counts for that month.
  • Reserve friendly. Private and semi-private rooms for crew who are here most nights. Bunks for line holders who are here a few nights a trip.
  • Keyless entry at any hour. A 1 am arrival off a late turn is normal here.

Who you will find in the house

Pilots at American Airlines, Envoy Air, SkyWest, PSA and other operations that run through DFW. Everyone keeps a permanent home elsewhere and uses the crashpad between trips, so the house stays quiet. Weekly professional cleaning keeps the kitchen, bathrooms and living areas in shape, and your bed is yours alone for your whole stay.

What it costs

Top bunks from $330 a month, bottom bunks from $380, semi-private rooms from $450 and private rooms from $475. All utilities, Wi-Fi, linens, weekly cleaning and parking are included. A $150 reservation fee holds your bed and is refundable after your first month.

Getting here from the airport

The house is 7.5 miles from DFW Airport. Most crew keep a car at the house (parking for 7 on the property) and drive to the employee lot; a rideshare from the terminal is a short trip if you do not. The exact address is shared once you are approved.

If you just got the base and need a bed before your first trip, apply today. Most new tenants are set up within a day or two: a short phone call, an online signature, and door access sent to your phone. Read what to look for in a crashpad if you are comparing options.

title: Cold Bed vs Hot Bed: How to Pick a Crashpad
excerpt: What a cold bed is, why it matters, and the questions to ask before you pay a crashpad deposit near any airport. Written by the people who run a cold-bed crashpad 7.5 miles from DFW.
content:
Crashpad listings all sound alike until you have slept in a bad one. Here is what the terms mean and what to ask before you send anyone a deposit.

Cold bed vs hot bed

A cold bed is yours for your whole stay. You leave your things on it, nobody else sleeps in it, and it is made up the way you left it. A hot bed is shared: you get whichever bed is open when you arrive, and someone else may have slept in it the night before. Hot beds are cheaper on paper. They are also why people stop using crashpads. Our house is cold beds only.

Questions to ask any crashpad

  1. How many people share a bathroom? Ask for the number of beds and bathrooms, not a vague "plenty."
  2. Who cleans, and how often? "Tenants take turns" means nobody. Look for a professional cleaner on a weekly schedule.
  3. What is the minimum stay and the notice period? Two or three months up front is common and bad for commuters whose base can change. One month, then month to month, is the fair version.
  4. What happens to my deposit? Get the refund terms in writing before you pay. Ours is a $150 reservation fee, refundable after the first month with notice by the 15th, and we put it in the agreement you sign.
  5. How do I get in at 1 am? Keys and lockboxes fail at the worst time. Keyless entry on your phone is the standard now.
  6. Where do I park? If the answer is "on the street somewhere," that is a problem on a 4 am show.
  7. Is it quiet? A crashpad full of other crew is quiet by default. A crashpad that also rents to non-crew is not.
  8. Is there a written agreement? A real agreement protects you as much as the owner. Walk away from a handshake deal.

What a fair deal looks like

  • Cold bed with a privacy curtain and a decent mattress
  • Linens and towel provided so you travel light
  • All utilities, Wi-Fi, laundry and parking included in one price
  • Weekly professional cleaning of the shared spaces
  • One-month minimum, month to month after, written notice terms
  • Keyless entry that is turned on before you arrive
